_note: SAMPLE INPUT ONLY. A teacher-style quiz used by the 'Try the sample class' button and the eval set. It contains questions and known misconceptions — never student responses or results.
title: Fractions check-in (sample)

questions.key_idea: Fractions need a common denominator before adding: 1/2 = 2/4, so 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

misconceptions.label: Adds tops and bottoms
misconceptions.signal_text: Adds the numerators together and the denominators together.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Use fraction strips to show halves and quarters must be the same size piece before adding.

misconceptions.label: Adds tops, keeps one bottom
misconceptions.signal_text: Adds the numerators without renaming 1/2 as 2/4.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Ask what 1/2 looks like in quarters before adding.

questions.prompt: Which is bigger: 1/3 or 1/5? Type the bigger fraction.
questions.key_idea: With the same numerator, a smaller denominator means bigger pieces, so 1/3 is bigger than 1/5.

misconceptions.label: Bigger denominator means bigger fraction
misconceptions.signal_text: Compares the denominators as whole numbers.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Share one pizza among 3 people, then among 5 — who gets more?

questions.key_idea: Find one quarter of 20 (20 ÷ 4 = 5), then take three quarters: 3 × 5 = 15.

misconceptions.label: Finds only one part
misconceptions.signal_text: Divides by the denominator but does not multiply by the numerator.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Draw 20 dots in 4 groups and circle three groups.

misconceptions.label: Divides by the numerator
misconceptions.signal_text: Uses the top number as the divisor.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Ask what the bottom number tells us about the groups.

questions.prompt: Write 0.6 as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.key_idea: 0.6 is six tenths, 6/10, which simplifies to 3/5 by dividing top and bottom by 2.

misconceptions.label: Does not simplify
misconceptions.signal_text: Converts to tenths correctly but stops before simplifying.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Ask for the biggest number that divides both 6 and 10.

misconceptions.label: Uses the digit as the denominator
misconceptions.signal_text: Reads the decimal digit as the bottom number.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Read 0.6 aloud as 'six tenths' and write what you hear.

questions.prompt: What is 2/3 × 3/4? Give your answer as a fraction.

misconceptions.label: Cross-multiplies
misconceptions.signal_text: Multiplies diagonally, as if comparing fractions.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Show 2/3 of a 3/4 strip with an area model.

questions.prompt: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Riya eats 3 slices. What fraction of the pizza is left?
questions.key_idea: 8 − 3 = 5 slices remain out of 8 equal slices, so 5/8 of the pizza is left.

misconceptions.label: Gives the fraction eaten
misconceptions.signal_text: Answers what was eaten instead of what is left.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Ask the student to re-read what the question asks for.

misconceptions.label: Compares part to part
misconceptions.signal_text: Uses slices left over slices eaten instead of over the whole pizza.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Ask what the bottom number of a fraction counts.

questions.key_idea: Dividing by 1/4 asks how many quarters fit into one half: two.

misconceptions.label: Multiplies instead of dividing
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Ask how many quarter-strips cover a half-strip.

misconceptions.label: Flips the wrong fraction
misconceptions.signal_text: Inverts the first fraction instead of the second.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Check the result with a picture: how many quarters are in a half?

questions.key_idea: 2/4 and 1/2 name the same amount: doubling the top and bottom keeps the value.

misconceptions.label: Different numbers mean different amounts
misconceptions.signal_text: Thinks equivalent fractions differ because the digits differ.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Fold a paper strip in half, then in half again.

questions.prompt: Put these in order from smallest to largest: 1/2, 2/5, 3/4
questions.key_idea: Compare by converting to a common form: 2/5 = 0.4, 1/2 = 0.5, 3/4 = 0.75.

misconceptions.label: Orders by denominator
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Place each fraction on a 0 to 1 number line.

misconceptions.label: Orders by numerator
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Place each fraction on a 0 to 1 number line.

misconceptions.label: Subtracts tops and bottoms
misconceptions.signal_text: Subtracts the numerators and the denominators separately.
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Use sixths strips to show the pieces must match.

misconceptions.label: Forgets to rename 1/3
misconceptions.remedy_hint: Ask how many sixths make one third.
